title: SLO economics mapping and runtime decision guide
author: Aisha Ramanathan
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines a repeatable approach to map service-level objectives (SLOs) and business economics into runtime routing and scaling decisions for Redwood’s inference platform. It provides concrete matrices, alert thresholds, dashboard templates, and an operational runbook so platform engineers and product owners can translate latency and cost targets into deterministic behavior at the edge, routing layer, and scheduler.

Intended audience
- Platform engineers (routing, scheduler, runtime)
- Product owners and SREs owning tenant SLAs
- Observability / cost tooling engineers

Scope and goals
- Map common SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability, correctness) to unit economics (cost/token, cost/response)
- Provide a decision matrix for routing (fast-path vs. bulk-path), fallback, and quantization/compact model downgrade policies
- Standardize alerts and dashboards to expose actionable signals for automated rollback and operator handoffs
- Include an operator runbook for emergent cost/latency tradeoffs

Why this matters
- Customers expect predictable latency but also want control over cost. Platform decisions that are opaque create surprising bills or unexpected degradation. This playbook ensures reproducible, observable translation from SLOs -> runtime policy -> billing impact.

Glossary (short)
- Fast-path: low-latency GPU/CPU pool optimized for latency-sensitive tokens (higher cost).
- Bulk-path: higher-throughput, lower-cost pool with relaxed latency (batching, longer queuing).
- Fallback policy: automatic downgrade to compatible model variant or queued execution when fast-path SLOs cannot be met.
- Token-unit: billing unit (single generated token).

SLO <-> economics baseline table
| SLO profile | p95 latency target | Cost priority | Default routing | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Interactive (chat) | 300ms | High | Fast-path (1x dedicated GPU slice) | Use prefix KV cache and prefix routing; never route to bulk-path by default |
| Worker (email digest, offline) | 3s | Low | Bulk-path (batched, CPU-friendly) | Favor quantized models, aggressive batching |
| Mixed (webhooks, user-initiated longer responses) | 800ms | Medium | Fast-path primary, bulk-path fallback | Use grace-period queue of 200ms before fallback |

Unit economics example assumptions (internal)
- Fast-path cost baseline: $0.00035 per token (includes GPU amortization, infra, SRE overhead)
- Bulk-path cost baseline: $0.00007 per token
- Average tokens per request: 120
- 1% p99 tail reduction via KV cache saves ~0.3 tokens per request on average

Decision matrix: routing and runtime actions
1) Admission control (edge):
   - Metric: in-flight requests / fast-path capacity; if > 0.85, divert new requests to queuing or apply headroom throttling.
   - Action: if p95 fast-path latency > target for 2 consecutive 60s windows -> enable 200ms grace queue and allow up to 10% of new requests to be routed to bulk-path.
2) Model downgrade (quality-preserving fallback):
   - When budget burn-rate > configured budget_saturation threshold (see config table) and p95 violation persists, switch interactive tenants to 8-bit quantized variant with A/B monitoring for quality drift.
3) Autoscaling signal selection:
   - Prefer throughput-weighted schedule (tokens/sec) for bulk-path, latency-based for fast-path.

Runtime configuration schema (reference)
| field | type | example | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| priority_profile | string | "interactive" | Maps to SLO profile above |
| fast_path_capacity_pct | integer | "70" | Percent of tenant quota reserved on fast-path |
| fallback_grace_ms | integer | "200" | How long to wait before fallback routing |
| budget_saturation_pct | integer | "85" | Percent of monthly committed budget consumed where aggressive cost controls apply |
| quantized_variant | string | "gptx-8q" | Compatible fallback model id |

Alert and dashboard patterns
- Primary SLO dashboard (per-tenant): p50/p95/p99 latency heatmap, tokens/sec, cost-per-1000-requests, dropped/queued rate.
- Cost-signal dashboard: rolling 24h burn-rate vs. committed quota, projected month-end spend at current burn-rate.
- Alerts (examples):
  - P95 latency > SLO for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows -> P95_Latency_Approaching_SLO (severity: P2).
  - Fast-path capacity utilization > 90% for 5 minutes -> FastPath_AtRisk (severity: P1).
  - Monthly burn-rate projection > 110% committed -> Budget_Exceeded_Predicted (severity: P0).

Alert rule examples (pseudo-PromQL)
- Fast-path utilization: avg_over_time(fast_path_utilization[5m]) > 0.9
- Burn-rate projection: sum_over_tenant(token_cost_last_24h) * 30 / 24 > committed_monthly_budget * 1.1

Automated remediation recipes
- Minor (P95 drift only):
  1. Run a traffic brief: snapshot current distribution (models/regions/seq_len).
  2. Enable grace queue (200ms) for affected tenants.
  3. Trigger on-call automated warm-up (spin up +20% fast-path workers for 10 minutes).
- Major (capacity saturation or budget breach):
  1. Initiate tenant-level throttling: reduce non-interactive token budgets by 50%.
  2. Enable model downgrade to quantized variant for non-A/B cohorts.
  3. Notify billing and customer success; prepare rollback plan.

Operator runbook: step-by-step (condensed)
1) Triage (first 5 minutes)
   - Check primary SLO dashboard and cost dashboard for correlating signals.
   - Run quick query: top 10 tenants by token/sec, top 10 models by p95 increase.
2) Contain (5–15 minutes)
   - If fast-path utilization > 92%: enable fast-path autoscale +20% surge for 15 minutes.
   - If burn-rate projection > 110%: enable tenant-level cost caps and trigger Budget_Exceeded_Predicted alert flow.
3) Mitigate (15–60 minutes)
   - Apply model downgrade for non-critical tenants.
   - If latency remains violated, consider regional routing to alternative region with spare capacity and notify customers of degraded latency with ETA.
4) Post-incident (within 72 hours)
   - Create a postmortem with traffic profile snapshots, decisions taken, and a recommended roadmap item if recurring.

Telemetry and instrumentation checklist
- Per-request: tenant_id, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, routing_path, kv_cache_hit, queue_wait_ms, worker_id.
- Aggregates: tokens/sec (1m/5m), p50/p95/p99 latencies, queue depth, fast-path utilization per-region.
- Cost attribution: cost per token by model variant and by routing_path; daily/weekly projection exports.

Dashboard template (short example instructions)
1. Create a multi-row dashboard titled: "SLO Economics — <tenant>"
2. Row 1: Latency heatmaps and p95 sparkline (time window 1h, step 30s)
3. Row 2: Token throughput + cost-per-1k-requests gauge with forecast annotation
4. Row 3: Routing breakdown (fast-path vs bulk-path) with percent and absolute tokens

Roadmap items (beyond scope)
- Q2 2026: Integrate budget projections into route decision engine for proactive throttling.
- Q3 2026: Per-tenant micro-A/B test harness to validate quantized variant quality before full rollout.
- Q4 2026: ML-driven prediction of short-term tail events for pre-warm scheduling.

Appendix A — Example tenant policy YAML
```yaml
tenant_policy_id: tenant-6421
priority_profile: interactive
fast_path_capacity_pct: 75
fallback_grace_ms: 200
budget_saturation_pct: 85
quantized_variant: gptx-8q
```

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets
- view burn-rate projection (internal): rdx metrics query "sum(token_cost_last_24h) * 30 / 24 by (tenant)"
- force enable grace queue for tenant: rdx control set-tenant-policy tenant-6421 --grace-ms 200 --force-apply
